strengths: Novel and effective perceptual loss formulation combining DINOv2 and SAM 2.1 that captures high-level semantics while avoiding pixel-level artifacts
Strong empirical results across quantitative metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) with demonstrated state-of-the-art or competitive performance on Ava-256 and NeRSemble benchmarks
Robust 3D consistency maintained across multiple viewing angles and extreme viewpoints, addressing a critical challenge in single-image 3D reconstruction
Elegant dual-task framework that handles both reconstruction and editing by encoder adaptation while reusing the core decoder, demonstrating good generalization
Comprehensive ablation studies validating each loss component and architectural choice, with clear analysis of contribution of different elements
Excellent qualitative results with convincing multi-view consistency and detailed 3D reconstructions across diverse subjects and poses
Practical contributions including interactive editing GUI and planned code release enhancing reproducibility and real-world applicability
Thorough supplementary material with extensive additional results, comparative analyses, and implementation details
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (Vision Transformers, DINOv2, SAM 2.1) without proposing fundamentally new algorithmic components
Incomplete baseline comparisons: missing comparisons with recent diffusion-based face synthesis and latent diffusion methods that could be competitive
Evaluation limited primarily to head-specific datasets; generalization to other 3D object categories and cross-dataset performance insufficiently explored
Significant editing limitations: explicitly acknowledges inability to handle expression transfer, requires segmentation/reference images, and shows artifacts in extreme scenarios
Loss function design lacks justification: CDI metric definition unclear in Eq. 5, equal loss weighting (λ=1.0) appears arbitrary, and SHP-CNN shows only marginal improvements despite added complexity
Missing quantitative identity preservation metrics: lacks face recognition distance measurements; relies primarily on ArcFace comparison with single baseline (NFE)
Insufficient failure case analysis: Section 4.6 mentions limitations but provides minimal visual examples or detailed analysis of breakdown scenarios
Computational cost underspecified: no inference time comparisons with baselines, memory requirements provided but training time and GPU scalability unclear
Method shows significant performance degradation when trained on 2D data only (Table 2), limiting applicability to domains lacking multi-view supervision
Multiple design choices lack ablation or justification: specific DINOv2 layer selection, PixelShuffle usage in decoder, architectural sensitivity analysis missing
